messages:
alex_w: Heads-up — seeing sporadic packet loss & 200-800ms east-west tails on gpu-pool-a (us-west-2) since ~03:10 UTC. Affected pods show RDMA disconnects and gRPC stalls. IPv6-only flows seem consistently worse. /cc @net-bot

maria_s: Can you paste output of `ip -6 route` and `ip -6 neigh` from one affected node?

alex_w: here from node-17 (trimmed):

```
$ ip -6 route
::/0 via fe80::1 dev eth0 proto static metric 100
2001:db8:20::/64 dev cni0 proto kernel metric 256
2001:db8:20:ff::/128 via fe80::febc:... dev eth0
2001:db8:20:ff::/128 via fe80::fd12:... dev toR1
```

$ ip -6 neigh show
2001:db8:20:ff::1 dev eth0 lladdr 3c:fd:fe:xx:xx:xx STALE
2001:db8:20:ff::1 dev toR1 lladdr 3c:fd:fe:yy:yy:yy STALE
```

ken_l: That double /128 for the same pod IP is red flag — we have host routes being advertised both by kube-proxy (eBPF) and by BGP from ToRs. Asymmetric return path + MTU differences = ICMPv6 frag issues.

sara_ops: kernel logs on node-17: "mlx5_core: skb dropped, IPv6 fragmentation offload not handled" — looks like mlx5 firmware + kernel offload interaction.

net-bot: fabric-monitor: jitter spike on us-west-2 fabric (03:11 UTC), packet-loss 0.8% between topo leaf-03 <-> leaf-04.

alex_w: Quick repro: `ping6 -M do -s 1400 2001:db8:20:ff::1` -> results: "Frag needed" and ~1-2% dropped. With -s 1200 it's stable.

ken_l: Workarounds we should try immediately: disable GRO/GSO/TSO for IPv6 on mlx5 NICs, and withdraw duplicate BGP host routes. Example commands:

```
# disable offloads for IPv6
ethtool -K eth0 gso off gro off tso off
# verify
ethtool -k eth0 | grep -i generic
```

maria_s: Also found config drift: ToR A has MTU 9000, ToR B shows 8986 after recent firmware change. That mismatch will definitely trigger "frag needed" for large payloads.

sara_ops: Note: kube-proxy currently does not SNAT IPv6 egress; if return path goes via ToR with host route, replies can be asymmetric. We need to pick a single authoritative host route source.

alex_w: For immediate mitigation I propose: 1) withdraw BGP host routes for the affected /128s (net team) 2) disable IPv6 offloads on sample nodes (ops) 3) revert ToR B MTU to 9000 (net) 4) monitor for 30m. If stable, re-enable one route source.

ken_l: Agreed. Also file a driver/kernel bug for mlx5 fragmentation offload on kernel 6.3 — observed similar symptoms in upstream: https://github.com/linux-fs/issue/xxxxx (placeholder).

maria_s: Plan and ETA: withdraw BGP host routes (5m), disable offloads on node-17 and node-23 (10m), fix ToR MTU (15m). Rolling checks on pods in gpu-pool-a.

alex_w: Running withdraw on a small prefix now (canary). Will push ethtool changes to node-17 after withdraw completes. Posting logs when done.

infra-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1789 (automated) — tags: ipv6, dual-stack, rdma, us-west-2, gpu-pool-a.

maria_s: After canary withdraw + offload disable: ping6 -s1400 shows no "Frag needed" and RDMA sessions recovered on node-17. CPU on node increased slightly (GSO off).

ken_l: Follow-up items: 1) enforce MTU drift detection in fabric CI 2) change BGP host-route policy to prefer kube-proxy origin for pod host routes 3) upstream bug report for mlx5 fragmentation offload 4) add IPv6 SNAT option for heavy-nat customers as fallback.

sara_ops: I'll file infra tasks and add runbook steps for disabling IPv6 offloads during incidents.

alex_w: Closing notes: workaround successful for now, will watch latency for next 24h. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
